root_cause.text: The ibmveth TSO/LSO path accepted GSO packets with MSS values below the physical adapter’s supported minimum, so the driver could pass unsupported small-MSS segmentation requests to hardware and trigger an adapter freeze.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `ndo_features_check` in `drivers/net/ethernet/ibm/ibmveth.c` to reject GSO when `skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_size < IBMVETH_MIN_LSO_MSS` (`224`), with the comment that “Some physical adapters do not support segmentation offload with MSS < 224” and that such packets previously “cause the adapter to freeze”; it also notes that only `gso_segs > 1` hits the problematic LSO path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a GSO feature check to disable unsupported small-MSS LSO packets and prevent adapter freezes.
intent_record.what: A new static function `ibmveth_features_check()` was added. It checks whether a packet is GSO, and if so whether `skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_size` is smaller than `IBMVETH_MIN_LSO_MSS`. When that condition is met, it emits a one-time warning with `netdev_warn_once()` and clears `NETIF_F_GSO_MASK` from the feature set. The function then returns `vlan_features_check(skb, features)`. The function is inserted before `ibmveth_netdev_ops`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packets that would use GSO/LSO with an MSS below the adapter's supported minimum are forced to fall back to non-GSO transmission. This prevents those packets from taking the hardware segmentation offload path, avoiding the described adapter freeze while still allowing normal transmission. VLAN feature filtering is preserved through the final `vlan_features_check()` call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add ibmveth feature-checking support so packet offload capabilities are validated correctly.
intent_record.what: A new net_device operation assignment was added to the ibmveth_netdev_ops structure: .ndo_features_check is now set to ibmveth_features_check.
intent_record.how: This causes the ibmveth driver to participate in the networking stack's feature compatibility checks for packets, allowing the driver to validate or restrict offload features at transmit time instead of relying solely on generic handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a constant for the minimum MSS required for LSO in the IBM veth driver.
intent_record.what: A new preprocessor macro named `IBMVETH_MIN_LSO_MSS` was added with the value `224` and an inline comment indicating it is the minimum MSS for LSO.
intent_record.how: This introduces a named constant that can be used elsewhere in the driver to enforce or compare against the minimum TCP MSS required for large segment offload, affecting any logic that relies on this threshold.

candidates.rationale: This appears to be part of the feature-check routine that, before the fix, returned success without rejecting unsupported GSO/LSO configurations. That allowed packets with MSS below the adapter minimum to reach hardware and could trigger the freeze described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix success return is from the GSO feature-check path that should have rejected unsupported small-MSS LSO/GSO configurations. By returning success unconditionally, the driver allowed such packets to proceed to hardware, matching the root cause that could trigger an adapter freeze.
